cards.explanation: The answer is smashing the pillars and tearing down the high places. The Israelites broke up the sacred pillars, chopped down the Asherah poles, and tore down the high places and altars. The text says they kept at it "…until they had utterly destroyed them all." They took the job seriously, friends, and that's a whole lot of demolition.

The answer is True. The verse says they tore these things down throughout Judah and Benjamin, "…as well as in Ephraim and Manasseh…" Four regions, one job, and the text says they didn't quit until it was all destroyed. That's a lot of ground to cover, friends.

The answer is singing praises at the gates. Hezekiah, king of Judah, set the divisions back up for the burnt offerings and peace offerings, for ministry, for giving thanks, and for singing praises at the gates of the LORD's dwelling. So praise was part of the job description, friends. Honestly, that's a better list than most of us have at work.

The answer is the king, from his own possessions. The text says the king contributed from his own possessions for the regular morning and evening burnt offerings, and for the Sabbaths, New Moons and appointed feasts. That came from Hezekiah's own possessions, not from somebody else's. It was all done as written in the Law of the LORD.

The answer is so they can devote themselves to the Law of the LORD. Hezekiah commanded the people in Jerusalem to make a contribution so the priests and Levites "…could devote themselves to the Law of the LORD." The gift is there so they can give themselves to that work. I like that, friends. It's like a friend covering your shift so you can finally get to the thing you've been trying to focus on.

The word is generously. The Israelites "…generously provided the firstfruits of the grain, new wine, oil, and honey…" Verse 5 adds that they brought in an abundance, a tithe of everything. I'd love to see that line at the front door, friends.

The answer is False. Verse 6 says the Israelites and Judahites living in the cities of Judah also brought a tithe of their herds and flocks. They brought a tithe of the holy things consecrated to the LORD their God too. So the giving reached well past Jerusalem, friends.

The answer is the seventh month. The text says they began building up the heaps in the third month and finished in the seventh. That's a long stretch of bringing and stacking, friends. I've waited a good while for a pan of cookies to cool when I wasn't paying attention.

The answer is that they bless the LORD and His people Israel. Hezekiah and his officials viewed the heaps, and they blessed the LORD and His people Israel. They blessed God and they blessed the people who brought the gifts. A pile that big deserves a big thank-you, friends.

The answer is that the LORD has blessed His people. Azariah, the chief priest of the household of Zadok, tells Hezekiah they've had enough to eat with plenty left over, "…because the LORD has blessed His people…" That's the reason he gives, friends. He points to the LORD.

The word is storerooms. Hezekiah commanded them to prepare storerooms in the house of the LORD, and they did so. When you've got heaps that big, friends, you need somewhere to put them. I once ran out of cooling racks, so I understand the pressure.

The answer is that he did what was good and upright and true. The writer says, "He did what was good and upright and true before the LORD his God." That's one sentence summing up everything he did throughout Judah. Honestly, friends, I'd take that written on my apron.

The answer is True. The text says Hezekiah "…acted with all his heart in every work that he began in the service of the house of God…" All his heart, every work, friends. I can't even finish one batch without sneaking a bite.
The answer is that he prospers. The text says he acted with all his heart "…in order to seek his God. And so he prospered." That's the outcome it gives, friends. I'll leave it right there.
